title: EPIC — Data accuracy and freshness

note.summary: This epic keeps every published amount, rule, form, phone number and date true on the day a user reads it. Its current outcome is Backlog because factual freshness is ongoing work.
note.goal: Keep every published amount, rule, form, phone number and date true on the day a user reads it.
note.whyItMatters: The product's largest ongoing risk is silent factual decay, not a missing feature; a wrong figure costs a disabled person money or a scarce appointment.
note.constraints: Use an actual official-source review before updating freshness, and do not add facts that are not verified.
doneWhen: Every published amount, rule, form, phone number and date is true on the day a user reads it.
note.priorityRationale: High because silent factual decay can cost a disabled person money or a scarce appointment.

title: EPIC — Coverage gaps and scope decisions

note.summary: This epic closes the remaining catalogue coverage questions that are genuinely scope decisions rather than research tasks. It also keeps already decided questions from being re-opened.
note.goal: Close the remaining catalogue coverage questions that are genuinely scope decisions rather than research tasks.
note.whyItMatters: Settled scope decisions must remain settled so completed coverage work is not repeatedly treated as a gap.
note.constraints: Treat Plan B placement and provincial child/family scope as the remaining questions, and keep Plan X closed.
doneWhen: The remaining catalogue scope questions are decided and already decided questions are not re-opened.
note.priorityRationale: Medium because the remaining work is limited to genuine catalogue scope decisions.

title: EPIC — Human accessibility and usability testing

note.summary: This epic covers the human accessibility and usability testing that has not yet happened. It is the sole remaining NO-GO condition.
note.goal: Have real screen-reader users and disabled participants complete journeys through the product and disposition the findings.
note.whyItMatters: No screen-reader user has ever completed a journey through this product, and automated checks cover roughly a third of real problems.
note.constraints: Human testing cannot be replaced by automated checks, and findings must be written as reproducible issues rather than broad redesign requests.
doneWhen: Human accessibility and usability testing has happened and every finding is dispositioned.
note.priorityRationale: High because this is the sole remaining NO-GO condition.

title: [DATA] Re-verify benefit figures before their freshness dates age out

note.summary: This backlog story keeps `BENEFIT_VERIFIED` tied to an actual official-source review. Every amount, cutoff, rule, form, phone number, processing time, application status and municipal detail must be checked against the current official page on the day of the change.
note.goal: Ensure no benefit record ages past its verification date without a same-day official-source review.
note.whyItMatters: A stale or unsupported figure can cost a disabled person money or a scarce appointment.
note.filesToTouch: TBD — verify against official source on the day
note.constraints: `BENEFIT_VERIFIED` is updated only after an actual official-source review. `canada.ca` returns 403 to automated fetch — read the CRA page in a real browser rather than trusting a search summary. Refuse a figure the official page does not state: the HATC has no percentage rate or maximum dollar credit in the record on purpose, and "$3,000" is a figure to refuse, not copy; `excise-gasoline-tax-refund` states no per-litre amount on purpose and gives the CRA number 1-877-432-5472 instead. Third-party figures have been wrong: BC RAHA's widely quoted $134,140 limit, the multigenerational credit's "15%" and "$7,500".
doneWhen: no record is past its verification date without a same-day official-source check
every changed figure has its source URL
a `DATA_CHANGELOG` entry exists for each fact change
note.priorityRationale: High because silent factual decay is the product's largest ongoing risk.

each checked entry has its date refreshed or its record corrected
note.priorityRationale: Medium because directory facts require recurring verification but the intake-status concern was disproved.

title: [DATA] Keep the data-change procedure enforced

note.summary: This backlog story keeps every data landing coupled to its required generators, changelog entry and browser-asset versioning. Generated files must continue to be produced by scripts rather than hand-edited.
note.goal: Enforce the complete data-change procedure on every relevant landing.
note.whyItMatters: The procedure prevents catalogue, guides, context, browser assets and documentation from drifting apart.
note.filesToTouch: public/grants-data.js; public/orgs-data.js; public/changelog.js; public/index.html; public/styles.css; src/**; public/guides/**; public/sitemap.xml; test/docs-consistency.test.js
note.readExactly: AGENTS.md, TASKVIEW-WORKFLOW.md, this ticket, public/changelog.js, public/index.html, public/styles.css, test/docs-consistency.test.js

title: [SCOPE] Decide where the PharmaCare Plan B long-term-care warning belongs

note.summary: This backlog decision concerns Plan B, which was verified 2026-07-29 but deliberately not built. The unresolved question is where to place the warning that a facility's Plan B registration should be checked before moving in.
note.goal: Record an owner decision on where the Plan B warning lives or that it is not carried.
note.whyItMatters: The questionnaire does not ask whether someone lives in long-term care, and no existing record provides a natural attachment point.
note.constraints: Verified facts: 100% of eligible prescription drugs and medical supplies for permanent residents of licensed long-term care facilities registered with Plan B; coverage is automatic on becoming a permanent resident, so like Plan F it has no application of its own; not all facilities are registered and the province suggests asking before moving in; it does not apply to extended-care, acute-care, multi-level or assisted-living facilities, nor to short-term or respite stays. The questionnaire never asks whether someone lives in long-term care, and there is no existing record to attach this to the way Plan F attached to `bc-at-home-medical`. Do not build before the scope decision.
doneWhen: an owner decision records where the warning lives, or that it is not carried
note.priorityRationale: Medium because the content is verified but needs an owner scope decision before it is built.

title: [SCOPE] PharmaCare Plan X stays closed — do not re-open

note.summary: This decision story is already closed as out of scope 2026-07-29 by owner decision. It remains on the board so Plan X is not re-opened on the mistaken premise that its enrolment route is unclear.
note.goal: Keep PharmaCare Plan X closed unless condition-specific records deliberately enter scope.
note.whyItMatters: The record preserves the actual scope reason and prevents settled work from being repeated.
note.constraints: Plan X has a real enrolment route: PharmaCare "cannot determine eligibility for the program or enrol individuals in it", and the BC Centre for Excellence in HIV/AIDS Drug Treatment Program does. It was excluded because it is condition-specific rather than disability-based, not because the route is unclear. If condition-specific records ever come into scope, re-verify against `bccfe.ca` — the `gov.bc.ca` page is a 2012 policy-manual entry last updated March 2025.

title: [PROCESS] Check the catalogue by record id before recording a coverage gap

note.summary: This backlog story makes catalogue lookup a required step before recording any new coverage gap. A 2026-07-29 re-audit found that five gap entries had been written without first reading the record that already covered them.
note.goal: Require record-id and keyword checks in `public/data.js` before any new coverage-gap entry.
note.whyItMatters: The check prevents duplicate research and false gap claims about coverage that already exists.
note.constraints: The five mistaken gaps were B.C. MSP Supplementary Benefits (shipped 2026-07-28 in `7b8e9db`), PharmaCare Plan P (shipped 2026-07-29), Plan F (no application of its own; MCFD submits the information, so it arrives with At Home Program enrolment), the B.C. annual earnings exemption (already in `bc-disability-assistance-pwd`'s note), and Plan S. The 2026-07-29 re-audit checked every remaining open item against `public/data.js` by record id and by keyword. Standalone per-plan PharmaCare URLs are unreliable — the Plan P one 404s — so read the section anchors on the `who-we-cover` hub instead.
doneWhen: the record-id and keyword check is stated as a required step before any new coverage-gap entry
note.priorityRationale: Low because this is a preventive process rule after the existing false gaps were identified.
